thread.title: S&P 500, Dow Jones Whacked; Buy These 3 Leading Growth Stocks?

author: DAVID SAITO-CHUNG
title: S&P 500, Dow Jones Whacked; Buy These 3 Leading Growth Stocks?
text:
Investors whacked stocks in the S&P 500 (down 1.2%) and the Dow Jones industrial average (off 1.6%) on Tuesday as financial markets fretted over the political situation in Italy and the risk that a new election in the third largest economy within the eurozone could have implications for the future of the key currency.
X Meanwhile, the Nasdaq composite suffered a smaller loss, down 0.5%. It continues to be the top index. At 7398, it's risen more than 7% since Jan. 1.
However, the 500 remains on track for a solid gain in May. With two trading sessions left in the month, the large-cap benchmark still holds a gain of roughly 1.6%.
The S&P SmallCap 600 continued to find buyers at the 1000 level as it bounced off a lighter intraday loss and edged only slightly lower by day's end.
At 1004, the 600 is up nearly 7.3% year to date, well ahead of the S&P 500's 0.6% advance.
Volume jumped on both main exchanges vs. Friday. That came as no surprise given that Friday's session was the dullest in trading activity in nearly two weeks. Still, the significant declines in higher turnover marks a distribution day, or bout of unusually intense institutional selling.

Please contact customer service CLOSE Meanwhile, President Trump's decision to resume tariffs on $50 billion worth of Chinese-made products shook Wall Street and sent some fund managers seeking a haven in U.S. Treasuries. The yield on the benchmark 10-year bond wilted to as low as 2.75%, hitting the lowest levels since April 11.
Breadth was negative as losing stocks topped winners by a nearly 10-7 margin on the NYSE. Yet computer and semiconductor-related stocks mostly held firm, and a few even broke out.
Micron Technology ( MU ) vaulted more than 4.2% at one point and hit a new high of 63.98. At that price, the data storage play briefly topped the 63.52 entry in a cup without handle.
In a cup without handle, the decline from head to toe should not exceed 33%. That's the same for any traditional cup-with-handle base pattern. The only difference: A stock might not make a final light pullback in price over a period of five sessions or more, and instead bolt past the cup's left-side peak.
Applied Materials ( AMAT ), the chip equipment giant, rallied more than 2%. Watch to see if the stock can keep rising and cross back above the long-term 200-day moving average.
Applied produced prodigious gains after it broke out of giant first-stage cup with handle at 21.77 in mid-May of 2016. The stock nearly tripled in price before going into cool-down mode these past 2-1/2 months.
Apple ( AAPL ), a member of IBD Leaderboard , surrendered just 0.4%.
Due to the smaller decline in the iPhone and iPad giant vs. the S&P 500, go to an IBD daily chart and you'll see that Apple's relative strength line continues to bump higher, a positive sign.
Apple shares currently stand slightly under 5% past a new buy point of 189.04. This means that investors can still buy the stock within the proper zone after a successful breakout.
